title: Comparing Your Real Options for The COREMERCH Sovereign Stack Deployment Guide — No Stripe Required
author: COREMERCH
excerpt: No KYC. No platform risk. No dependency. Revenue flows to a wallet you control. The infrastructure layer that makes platforms optional.
imageAlt: Sovereign commerce stack ownership — no platform dependency — for digital creators in Bangladesh
imageCaption: You own the storefront, the customer list, the order history, and the wallet. COREMERCH has no access after deployment.

content.text: Every platform account you depend on is a risk you are carrying on someone else's terms. PayPal can freeze your balance with no warning and hold it for 180 days. Stripe can reject your application because your country is on an internal risk list they will never show you. Gumroad can suspend your store because an algorithm flagged your content category. These events happen to thousands of [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-creators-ghana-get-paid-online-broken-here|creators]] every month — disproportionately in Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Kenya, Ethiopia, and other markets that conventional [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-payment-methods-filipino-digital-creators-complete-infrastructure|COREMERCH guide to payment]] platforms treat as high-risk by default. Sovereign [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/full-infrastructure-guide-payment-infrastructure-south-asian-creators|The Full]] means the storefront code is in your GitHub or Cloudflare account. The customer list is in your Supabase database or Google Sheet. The order history is exportable as CSV at any time. The product files are in your Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. The wallet addresses and all funds were never touched by anyone else. COREMERCH has no access after deployment.
What Each Option Actually Offers

The KYC requirement — Know Your Customer identity verification — is the mechanism through which conventional payment platforms enforce geographic restrictions. To open a Stripe account, you need a government-issued ID from a supported country, a bank account in that country, and a registered business entity in some cases. If any element is from a country on Stripe's unsupported list, the application fails. NOWPayments requires no KYC from merchants. There is no identity verification, no document upload, no bank account requirement, and no geographic restriction on who can create a merchant account. Your buyers also do not need to create an account, verify their identity, or provide personal information to complete a purchase.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Platform suspension risk is asymmetric in a specific way that most creators only understand after experiencing it. When a PayPal or Stripe account is functioning normally, the risk feels theoretical and distant. When the platform acts — through automated risk flagging, policy enforcement, or geographic restriction tightening — the creator loses their revenue channel immediately. Funds inside the platform may be held for up to 180 days. The appeals process rarely reverses these decisions. Sovereign infrastructure removes this asymmetry completely. Your Cloudflare Pages store cannot be suspended by a payment processor. Your wallet cannot be frozen by a platform's compliance team.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Self-custody means holding crypto in a wallet where you control the private keys — not in an exchange account, not in a payment processor's custodial system, but in a wallet where only you can authorize transactions. MetaMask, Trust Wallet, and hardware wallets like Ledger are common options for different security levels and use cases. When digital store revenue flows into a self-custody wallet, no company can freeze it, no regulator can direct a platform to hold it, and no compliance algorithm can flag it for review. COREMERCH configures NOWPayments to route all payments directly to the wallet addresses you provide during setup.
A wallet you control cannot be frozen by anyone — that is the fundamental difference from a platform account balance.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

The ownership structure of a COREMERCH deployment is explicit and verifiable. After any deployment, the customer holds all of the following under their own accounts: the storefront code in their GitHub or Cloudflare account, the customer email list in their Supabase database or Google Sheet, the order and payment history exportable as CSV at any time, the product files in their Google Drive or Cloudflare R2, the NOWPayments account set up under their email address, all wallet addresses and the funds inside them. COREMERCH has zero access to any of these after delivery.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

The practical steps to infrastructure sovereignty start with choosing where your data lives. In Stack 01, orders are stored in Google Sheets — your Google account, your data, exportable at any time. In Stack 02, orders are stored in Supabase — your Supabase account, PostgreSQL database, full SQL access, exportable at any time. Product files in Stack 01 live in Google Drive — your Google account, 15GB free, shared via time-limited links generated by Apps Script. In Stack 02, files live in Cloudflare R2 — your Cloudflare account, 10GB free, zero egress fees, presigned URLs with configurable expiry.
The Complete Technical Architecture Reference

The long-term case for sovereign infrastructure is not just about avoiding platform suspensions — it is about compounding ownership over time. Every order that flows through your sovereign stack adds an entry to a database you own. Every buyer email address is in a list you control and can export at any time. Every transaction hash is cryptographic proof of revenue that no platform can dispute or withhold. Over months and years, this accumulates into a complete business record that you own unconditionally. Platform-dependent businesses lose all of this the moment the platform changes its terms, restricts their market, or suspends their account.
Advanced Configuration and Scaling Considerations

The KYC requirement — Know Your Customer identity verification — is the mechanism through which conventional payment platforms enforce geographic restrictions. To open a Stripe account, you need a government-issued ID from a supported country, a bank account in that country, and a registered business entity in some cases. If any element is from a country on Stripe's unsupported list, the application fails. NOWPayments requires no KYC from merchants. There is no identity verification, no document upload, no bank account requirement, and no geographic restriction on who can create a merchant account. Your buyers also do not need to create an account, verify their identity, or provide personal information to complete a purchase.
What does sovereign commerce infrastructure mean for digital creators?

Sovereign infrastructure means the creator owns every component of their commerce operation — not as a policy promise, but as a technical reality. The storefront code is in your GitHub or Cloudflare account. The customer email list is in your Supabase database or Google Sheet. The order and payment history is exportable as CSV at any time from your own database. The product files are in your Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. The NOWPayments account is registered under your email address. The wallet addresses and all funds inside them were never touched by COREMERCH. COREMERCH has no access after delivery.
No KYC means no geographic gatekeeping — anyone in the world can pay you without creating an account or verifying identity.
Related: How Creators Like You Are Building Sovereign Stores

Creators researching infrastructure ownership and no-KYC payment options are typically at a turning point — ready to build on infrastructure they control after experiencing or observing the asymmetric risk of platform dependency. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 is the complete sovereign deployment: Cloudflare Pages, Workers, Supabase, and NOWPayments, all under your accounts, end-to-end tested before handoff. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents the complete build process for both Stack 01 and Stack 02 for creators who want to self-deploy. COREMERCH has no access after delivery. See both at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Move any existing revenue out of platform custodial accounts and into a self-custody wallet you control — Trust Wallet for mobile, MetaMask for browser, hardware wallet for larger amounts. Create a NOWPayments account and configure it with your self-custody wallet addresses — funds route directly to your wallet on every transaction with no platform holding period. Deploy your sovereign stack under your own accounts — GitHub or Cloudflare, your choice of database, your NOWPayments API key, your delivery email service. Confirm that your order database gives you an independent transaction record that does not depend on any platform's continued operation. Complete a mainnet test transaction and verify the complete pipeline before promoting.
